criteria.text: The participant is at least 18 years old and has provided informed consent.
The participant has an Eastern Cooperative Oncology Group (ECOG) performance status of 0 or 1.
The participant has pathologically confirmed NSCLC, either locally advanced or metastatic, not amenable to curative surgery or radiotherapy.
The participant has measurable disease per RECIST v1.1.
The participant has adequate organ function (bone marrow, liver, kidney, coagulation).
The participant has received one to two prior lines of therapy including an anti-PD-1/anti-PD(L)-1 agent and platinum-based chemotherapy.
The participant has a documented RAS mutation status, defined as Nonsynonymous mutations in KRAS, NRAS, or HRAS at codons 12, 13, or 61 (G12, G13, or Q61).
The participant is able to take oral medications.
The participant has received prior therapy with direct RAS-targeted therapy or docetaxel.
The participant has untreated central nervous system (CNS) metastases.
The participant has medically significant comorbidities (significant cardiovascular disease, lung disease, or impaired GI function).
The participant is receiving ongoing anticancer therapy.
The participant is pregnant or breastfeeding.

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: These questions are about the trial "Study of Daraxonrasib (RMC-6236) in Patients With RAS Mutated NSCLC (RASolve 301)". Your earlier answers already covered 6 of its rules. I'll ask about the rest of its rules one at a time. You can skip any question, and "I don't know" is always fine.

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: Are you 18 years of age or older?

transcript.speaker: participant
transcript.text: Yes, I'm 58.

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: Thanks. Are you willing to sign an informed consent form if you decide to join the study?

transcript.speaker: participant
transcript.text: Yes, I'm organized and keep a folder of every report, so I'm willing to sign the informed consent form.

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: Thanks. Have you had recent blood tests to check that your bone marrow, liver, kidney, and blood clotting functions are adequate?

transcript.speaker: participant
transcript.text: I don't know. I keep a folder of reports, but I don't have the specific recent blood test results for bone marrow, liver, kidney, and clotting functions handy right now.

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: Do you have a recent pathology or genetic test report that confirms a RAS mutation (specifically in the KRAS, NRAS, or HRAS genes)?

transcript.speaker: participant
transcript.text: My report says KRAS was not detected. I don't know about NRAS or HRAS.

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: Thanks. Do you have any recent test results that show whether you have a mutation in the NRAS or HRAS genes?

transcript.speaker: participant
transcript.text: I don't know. I don't have those specific results for NRAS or HRAS handy.

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: Thanks. Are you able to take medications by mouth?

transcript.speaker: participant
transcript.text: Yes, I take Tagrisso by mouth every day, so I can definitely take medications by mouth.

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: Have you ever received treatment specifically targeting the RAS protein, or have you taken a chemotherapy drug called docetaxel?

transcript.speaker: participant
transcript.text: I haven't had any treatment targeting the RAS protein. I also haven't had docetaxel; I've only had Tagrisso and radiation.

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: Thanks. Do you have any significant heart, lung, or stomach/intestine conditions that your doctor considers serious?

transcript.speaker: participant
transcript.text: No heart problems. I've never had lung inflammation or scarring, and I don't have any stomach or intestine conditions.

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: Are you currently receiving any ongoing anticancer therapy, such as chemotherapy, immunotherapy, or targeted treatment?

transcript.speaker: participant
transcript.text: Yes, I am currently taking Tagrisso, which is a targeted treatment pill, every day.

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: Thank you, that's all my questions. Your record for this trial is ready, for you and your oncologist. They and the trial team decide whether it is right for you.
